messages.content: Write the introduction to a guide for a REST API that manages calendar bookings. Around 200 words.

## Introduction

This guide covers the Booking API, a REST interface for managing calendar bookings: creating them, checking availability, updating times, and canceling when plans change. The API is organized around a few core resources: calendars, time slots, and bookings. Each calendar represents a bookable resource, such as a room, a piece of equipment, or a person's schedule. Time slots define when that resource is open for booking, and bookings represent a confirmed reservation against one of those slots.

Every request and response uses JSON, authentication happens via a bearer token in the Authorization header, and all endpoints live under a versioned base path so future changes don't break your existing integration. The sections that follow walk through authentication, then the core endpoints for listing availability, creating a booking, retrieving or modifying an existing one, and canceling.

Along the way you'll find example requests and responses, a list of error codes and what triggers them, and notes on rate limits and pagination.

If you're integrating a scheduling tool, a booking widget, or an internal ops dashboard, start with the Authentication section, then move to Creating a Booking: the endpoint most integrations touch first. Everything else builds on the same patterns you'll see there.

All requests to the API require a bearer token, obtained by exchanging your client credentials at the `/oauth/token` endpoint. Include this token in the `Authorization` header of every call using the `Bearer` scheme; requests without a valid token receive a `401 Unauthorized` response. Tokens expire after one hour, so integrations should refresh them proactively rather than waiting for a failed request. Each token is scoped to a specific calendar or set of calendars, so a booking widget tied to one room can't read or modify another team's schedule. If you're building a server-side integration, keep your client secret out of source control and out of any code that ships to a browser; use a backend endpoint to mint short-lived tokens for client-side use instead.
Rewrite it for someone who has never used a REST API before.

output:
## Introduction

This guide explains how to use the Booking API to manage calendar bookings over the internet.

You don't need to know much about programming to follow along, but you should be comfortable copying commands and reading examples. A REST API is just a way for two computer programs to talk to each other by sending messages back and forth, usually in a format called JSON, which looks a lot like a list of labeled values (for example, `"date": "2026-09-10"`).

With this API you can do four main things: check when a room, a piece of equipment, or a person is free, create a new booking, look up or change a booking you already made, and cancel one you no longer need.

Every action in this guide happens by sending a request to a specific web address (called an endpoint) and getting a response back that tells you what happened. Think of it like filling out a form and mailing it in, then getting a reply in the mail confirming what was done.

The rest of this guide walks through each step in order: first how to prove who you are (authentication), then how to check availability, and then how to create your first booking. Start at the top and work down. Each section includes a full example you can copy and adjust.
